title: A textbook example puts a 1 kilogram mass at about 1.7 newtons on the Moon
summary: OpenStax Physics prints a Moon example in which a 1 kilogram mass weighs about 1.7 newtons, against 9.8 newtons on Earth.
body: OpenStax Physics says gravity varies slightly from place to place on Earth, and varies a great deal away from Earth. In the example on the second-law page, acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is given as 1.67 metres per second squared, so a 1.0 kilogram mass weighs 9.8 newtons on Earth and only about 1.7 newtons on the Moon in that example. A NASA Moon fact sheet is a different card and is not copied here. The book date is 26 March 2020. The figures are the textbook's example, not a new measurement.

sources.title: 4.3 Newton's Second Law of Motion
sources.author: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs
sources.note: Paraphrase only, not a quotation. OpenStax Physics, Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, published 26 March 2020. The assigned licence for /books/physics/ is CC BY 4.0; the page footer also prints a noncommercial clause, so this card does not copy the sentence. Supports the printed Moon example: 1.67 m/s^2, and about 1.7 N versus 9.8 N for a 1.0 kg mass.
